# The Spoken Proof

## Core law

> status: ratified (D-0003, D-0006, D-0180)

A spell is a literal, rigorous logical proof, spoken aloud — rigorous in the sense that
it could, in principle, be formally encoded (the author's benchmark: "encodable in
lean"), yet dressed entirely in pre-modern scholasticism and ancient jurisprudence. The
speaking of proof IS the story's "battle" element: confrontations are resolved by
constructing and voicing a flawless chain from the world's standing premises to a
conclusion the world must then honor. A flawed premise, a gap, a fallacy — the proof
fails, and failure has consequences. There is deep lore in the corpus of known
theorems, and the verbal element is highly structured, never mystical hand-waving.
There is one working magic: lawful proof over Wyrd-and-Frith. The other apparent
"magics" are interfaces into that law, not rival systems.

## Hard-magic discipline, hard-SF spirit

> status: ratified (D-0004, D-0027, D-0180)

The system obeys three commitments. First: strictly pre-modern presentation — medieval
or earlier; no modern technology anywhere in the literal world. Second: true hard
magic, spiritually related to hard SF — rules are consistent, consequences derivable,
limits real. Third: the growth-of-human-ability model (Dune, not D&D). Power is not
gathered from outside; it is trained, disciplined human capacity — and the story
deliberately contrasts three registers: **the rules of the world** (fixed, ancient,
discoverable), **the stuff humans make** (tools, records, crafts — finite and
craftable), and **the unbounded growth potential of humans** unlocked through deep
application.
This hard-magic promise is pedagogical as well as mechanical: any proof-work that
solves a plot problem must be taught, repeated, and bounded before the story spends it.

## Extended cognition: artifacts as mind

> status: ratified (D-0028, D-0180)

All paper artifacts — books, oracle decks, even scraps — are extensions of human memory
and reasoning power. Casting complex proofs exceeds any single skull's working memory;
the tools hold premises so the mind can hold the argument. This is also why
cooperative teams accomplish what no isolated genius can: a group that trusts each
other can distribute a proof across several minds and the artifacts passing between
them. See [[artifacts-and-memory]] and [[megaliths-and-leys]] for the full ladder of
scale, from a scrap of vellum to a standing circle.
In the approved architecture, those artifacts are **holders** and **maps** for
premises: they help find, order, remember, check, distribute, time, or witness proof.
They do not cast by themselves.

## The cost

> status: provisional (D-0072, D-0180)

The session's working model of cost, approved directionally: casting burns cognition
and body. Holding a large proof means holding the local world in working memory — soil
composition, water weight, the history of a treaty — and an error or overload rebounds
as physiological damage: nosebleeds, collapse, memory scars, in the worst cases
madness. Casting is hungry work (fat and honey matter; see [[economy]]). There are no
glowing effects: from the outside, high magic looks like a person standing very still
in the mud, sweating, speaking with terrible precision. The toll is the drama.
The existence of bodily/cognitive cost is load-bearing; the exact cost schedule,
failure taxonomy, and episode-by-episode teaching ladder remain extension work.

## The chorus: distributed proof-speaking

> status: provisional (D-0072, D-0180)

Approved with the note that the proprietary-versus-open-knowledge allegory lands well:
when a working exceeds one mind, a practiced circle divides the argument — one holds
the architecture, another the local premises, another the physical anchors — passing
variables through cards, knots, and spoken hand-offs. This demands radical trust; a
hidden agenda or broken focus snaps the chain and the backlash lands on everyone. The
empire cannot replicate this: its hierarchy of hoarded knowledge and mutual suspicion
caps what its scribes can jointly hold, while a community that teaches freely raises
its ceiling with every student. See [[information-control]].
The architecture is approved as a single-system interface: cards, knots, animals,
circles, local experts, and spoken hand-offs distribute one proof rather than combining
different powers.

## Intent and corruption

> status: proposed

A suggested mechanic never ruled on: proofs spoken in malice or greed curdle — the Wyrd
rejects arguments whose premises include the speaker's own domination, making cold
clarity or radical empathy a computational requirement, and brute aggression literally
powerless. Do not assert; do not contradict.

## What magic is not

> status: rejected (D-0002, D-0180)

No musical, harmonic, or acoustic-resonance magic mechanics — no monochords, no
frequency-matching, no song-as-spell. (Music exists richly in the world's culture and
in the show's score — see [[audio-design]] — it just isn't the mechanism of magic.)
Prophecy, destiny, vague intention, elemental power, violence, and moral purity are
also not working magic. If intent matters later, it must matter through premise
quality, consent, scope, or reciprocity, never as a free-floating fuel source.

## The music clause

> status: ratified (D-0146)

Rites and remembrances may carry song, drum, and dance — as culture, and as the
show's score — but music is never the working magic. The working magic remains the
spoken proof (D-0002 stands untouched). A funeral may be sung; the ward is argued.
The distinction is load-bearing: it keeps the world's liturgy warm and human while
the magic stays rigorous, and it is the rule that lets seasonal and remembrance
rite flourish (D-0146) without reopening the rejected musical-magic door.

## The proof-speech register

> status: ratified (D-0166)

A spoken proof is the Concordance: each premise carried by a different surfaced
voice's clean diction — the scribe's clipped accounting, the keener's cadence, the
weaver's litotes — converging in Enfys's own blended close. Beneath it runs the
Spoken-Ledger scaffold: plain declarative chain, the refrain of assent ("Say so."),
the close that names what is now held. A small stock of attested loan-word binders
marks the joints of a proof — old fossil words, never a conlang — grown one term at
a time through the naming oracle. The proof register is its own silhouette: nobody
else in the world speaks this way, and when it begins, the listener knows.

## Timing: tide and moon

> status: ratified (D-0146)

Ward-and-knot craft is timed as well as worded: certain wards seat only at their hour — slack
tide, the dark of the moon, the turn of a season — so *when* a knot is tied is a premise like
any other, and a ward can fail for being made at the wrong hour as surely as for the wrong
fibre (which deepens the opening ward-knot without changing it, [[apprentice]], D-0113). Timing
is craft-discipline, the kind of derivable constraint the hard magic wants. The moon governs
tides and hours, never destiny: there is no astrology-as-fate here, because the Wyrd is
consequence and not prophecy. The moon-count also rhymes across the world without being forced —
the same turning that seats a ward runs the Turning's twenty-nine leaves, one for each night of
the moon ([[the-turning]], D-0148).
